public_rationale: The sources document AI spam and its reach, but do not establish that it predominated across Facebook when Zitron wrote. His linked report includes a 22% result from one account in an earlier period. That cannot support platform-wide dominance, but it also cannot disprove it in January 2025.
limitations: Personalized feeds can differ substantially between users.
The majority-exposure interpretation makes an undefined term testable; a looser meaning of dominates could lead to a different assessment.
Both evidence items concern earlier periods and are context only.

statement.excerpt: AI-generated slop already dominates the platform, and as discussed earlier, the quality of the platform has fallen into utter disrepair, mostly because Meta's only concern is keeping you on the platform to show you ads or content it’s been paid to show you, even if the reason you're seeing it is because you can't find the stuff you actually want to find.

our_interpretation: Assess the supplied normalized proposition, excluding the surrounding claims about Meta's motives and platform quality.
The ordinary reading of dominates is that low-quality AI-generated material makes up most content users encounter in Facebook feeds. For measurement, most means more than half of feed exposures.

Because already describes the current state without a reporting period, use January 1–17, 2025, through publication. This is the immediately preceding period that contemporaneous feed observations could describe.
A sample of selected spam pages or one person's personalized feed cannot establish platform-wide predominance.
criteria.support_condition: Representative measurements for the target period show that low-quality AI-generated content accounted for more than half of Facebook feed exposures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative measurements for the target period show that such content accounted for half or less of Facebook feed exposures, with uncertainty sufficiently small to distinguish the result.

evidence.explanation: The report describes an investigation published in June using one account and more than a thousand posts. Its 22% finding cautions against treating this linked article as proof of majority prevalence; the underlying primary measurement was not independently retrieved.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative audit of Facebook feed exposures during the target period, with reliable AI-content classification and a disclosed quality definition.
